snippet: Implied volatility alone accounts for four fifths of the average long-short return, and for nearly all of it on the two rollover days; among stocks of similar volatility, the idiosyncratic-volatility and maximum-return anomalies point the other way. What the expiration weekend costs the holder of a contract that does not expire, beyond what any weekend costs, is not time decay or realized variance but a missing recovery in implied volatility, the rise that every other weekend shows and this one does not; it grows with volatility and with the open interest that rolls.
